tagline: Up through the Pisgah, where American forestry went to school.
intro: US 276 starts at the stone pillars a few miles east of Brevard that mark the edge of the Pisgah National Forest and climbs north past Looking Glass Falls and Sliding Rock to the Pink Beds, an upland bog grown thick with rhododendron and laurel. From there it switchbacks up to the Blue Ridge Parkway at Wagon Road Gap, passes beneath it, and comes down the East Fork of the Pigeon River to Woodrow.

At Woodrow NC 215 turns back south past Lake Logan, tops out at Beech Gap at 5,335 feet, and follows the North Fork of the French Broad down to Rosman. Much of the road was laid on old logging railroad grades.

moments.title: Looking Glass Falls
moments.text: The falls drop 60 feet right beside the road, and in 1990 a kayaker went over them successfully and hurt his back doing it.

moments.title: Sliding Rock
moments.text: Looking Glass Creek runs down about 60 feet of gently sloping rock into a pool some eight feet deep and near 55 degrees all year, and visitors follow it down.

moments.title: Cradle of Forestry
moments.text: Carl Schenck's forestry students summered at the Pink Beds in cabins with names like Hell Hole, Little Bohemia, The Palace and Rest for the Wicked.

practical: Tractor-trailers are barred, and with grades of 9 percent the road is not recommended for RVs or buses.
